name: Proximal Myopathy with Focal Depletion of Mitochondria

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proximal Myopathy Mitochondrial Depletion Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of symmetrical proximal muscle weakness predominantly affecting limb girdles
Muscle biopsy demonstrating focal depletion of mitochondria on histochemical and ultrastructural analysis
Mild to moderate elevation of serum creatine kinase levels
Identification of pathogenic variants in mitochondrial DNA maintenance genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of symmetrical proximal muscle weakness plus muscle biopsy showing focal mitochondrial depletion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing and serum biomarkers support diagnosis but are not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Symmetrical proximal limb girdle muscle weakness
searchTerms: weakness in shoulder and hip muscles
symmetrical upper and lower limb weakness
proximal muscle weakness on both sides

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal depletion of mitochondria in muscle fibers
searchTerms: loss of mitochondria in muscle cells

common.symptomName: Exercise intolerance with early muscle fatigue
Mild elevation of serum creatine kinase

searchTerms: muscle aches in upper arms and thighs
pain in shoulder and hip muscles

occasional.symptomName: Dysphagia due to oropharyngeal muscle involvement

rare.symptomName: Rhabdomyolysis episodes triggered by exercise or infection
searchTerms: muscle breakdown after exercise or infection
episodes of muscle damage triggered by activity

rare.symptomName: Cognitive impairment related to mitochondrial dysfunction
searchTerms: cognitive difficulties due to energy problems

laboratory: Mild to moderate elevation of serum creatine kinase
Lactate elevation in blood or CSF during exercise or stress
imaging: Muscle MRI showing selective involvement of proximal muscles with fatty infiltration
Cardiac MRI may reveal conduction system abnormalities or cardiomyopathy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in mitochondrial DNA maintenance genes such as POLG, TK2, or others
other: Muscle biopsy demonstrating focal mitochondrial depletion by histochemical stains (e.g., COX, SDH)
Electron microscopy showing reduced mitochondrial number and abnormal morphology

distinguishingFeatures: Diffuse rather than focal mitochondrial abnormalities on biopsy
More systemic involvement including CNS and multisystem features
Genetic mutations in sarcoglycan or dystrophin-related genes
Absence of mitochondrial depletion on muscle biopsy
Presence of inflammatory infiltrates on muscle biopsy
Elevated inflammatory markers and response to immunosuppressive therapy

redFlags: Episodes of rhabdomyolysis with acute renal failure
